paragraphs.source_en: Tofu said, “Sir, it is only natural that you should not understand it. For the new poetry of ten years ago and the new poetry of today are quite different; it has advanced at a tremendous pace. Recent poems are absolutely impossible to understand if you read them lying in bed, or while waiting for a train at a station. Even the person who wrote the poem is often at a loss for an answer when questioned about it. Since it is written entirely by inspiration, the poet bears no responsibility beyond that. Annotations and explanations are the business of scholars; they have nothing whatever to do with us. The other day, a friend of mine, a man named Soseki, wrote a short story entitled One Night, and whoever read it found it vague and misty, with no idea what the author meant to say. Someone therefore went to the author himself and solemnly asked what purpose the work had, but he said, ‘That sort of thing is no concern of mine.’ He would not take the matter up at all. I think that is precisely where the poet’s special character reveals itself.”
